    Mo
     is a critically acclaimed, Peabody Award-winning Netflix comedy-drama series created by and starring comedian Mo Amer, which ran for two seasons (2022–2025) and is available to stream on Netflix. The show is a semi-autobiographical, heartfelt, and humorous look at a Palestinian refugee's life in Texas. 
    This video features an interview with Mo Amer about his hit Netflix series:
    59s
    CBS Mornings
    YouTube• Apr 1, 2025
    • Why was it "canceled"? Mo was not canceled due to poor performance; rather, it was announced in January 2023 that it was renewed for a second and final season, which premiered on January 30, 2025, to widespread acclaim.
    • Watch
      Mo:
      You can stream both seasons of the show on Netflix.
       
    The series is praised for its raw storytelling and for shedding light on real-life experiences with humor, according to IMDb user reviews.

    Is Mo on Netflix a true story?
    Created and executive produced by Amer and his Ramy co-star Ramy Youssef, Mo is a semi-autobiographical series inspired by Amer's life as a Palestinian refugee growing up in Houston. Amer plays Mo Najjar, a man who's learning to adapt to his new world as he embarks on the path to US citizenship.

    Description

    Mo Najjar straddles the line between two cultures, three languages and a ton of foolishness as a Palestinian refugee constantly living one step away from asylum on the path to U.S. citizenship.
    Starring: Mo Amer; Farah Busies; Teresa Ruiz; Tobe Nwigwe; Omar Elba
    No. of episodes: 16
    Writers: Mohammed Amer, Ramy Youssef, Anna Salinas
    Program creators: Mohammed Amer, Ramy Youssef
    First episode date: August 24, 2022 (USA)
